title: reverse_proxy with versions 3 silently ignores tls_trust_pool and verifies against the system roots
body:
### Issue Details

Fixes https://github.com/caddyserver/caddy/issues/8041

A reverse_proxy that speaks HTTP/3 to its upstream ignores the CA configured with `tls_trust_pool`.

Every dial fails with x509: certificate signed by unknown authority, because the HTTP/3 transport is built with `RootCAs == nil` and Go falls back to the system trust store. I have populated our Certs to this to make it work for now.

The same proxy without versions 3 honours the trust pool correctly, which makes this look like a certificate problem rather than a config one.

Minimal reproduction:

An upstream serving HTTP/3 with a certificate from a private CA:

```caddyfile
site.internal {
      reverse_proxy backend:4001 {
              transport http {
                      tls
                      tls_server_name backend
                      tls_trust_pool file /tls/myRootCa.crt
                      versions 3
              }
      }
}
```

- Expected: the upstream's certificate verifies against `/tls/myRootCa.crt`.
- Actual: tls: failed to verify certificate: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority. Dropping versions 3 (so the proxy uses HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2) makes the identical config work.

The running config still shows the pool, which is what makes this hard to spot. 

`GET /config/` returns:
```json
{"protocol":"http","tls":{"ca":{"pem_files":["/tls/myRootCa.crt"],"provider":"file"},"server_name":"backend"},"versions":["3"]}
```
Cause (Per my best guess)

`HTTPTransport.NewTransport` calls `MakeTLSClientConfig` twice:

// modules/caddyhttp/reverseproxy/httptransport.go:422 for the HTTP/1.1+2 transport
`rt.TLSClientConfig, err = h.TLS.MakeTLSClientConfig(caddyCtx)`

// modules/caddyhttp/reverseproxy/httptransport.go:507 for the HTTP/3 transport
`h.h3Transport.TLSClientConfig, err = h.TLS.MakeTLSClientConfig(caddyCtx)`

`MakeTLSClientConfig` reaches the trust pool through `ctx.LoadModule(t, "CARaw")` and `LoadModuleclears` the raw field on its way out.

So on the second call `t.CARaw` is `nil`, the `cfg.RootCAs = ca.CertPool()` branch is skipped, and the HTTP/3 transport gets a config with no roots and falls back.

The cost falls entirely on the HTTP/3 path, because RoundTrip prefers h3Transport whenever it exists (`httptransport.go:648`). The transport that received the trust pool is never used for requests, the one that serves every request is the one that lost it.

Module-backed fields are the only ones affected: `server_name`, `insecure_skip_verify` and `theclient-certificate` paths are plain struct fields and survive both calls.

Build the client config once and give the HTTP/3 transport a clone, rather than calling `MakeTLSClientConfig` a second time.

Environment

Reproduced on a build from master (September 2026), Alpine container, Go's system roots without the private CA installed. Both call sites and the `LoadModule` reset are unchanged in current master.


## Assistance Disclosure
Claude to trace down the bug and testing. Implementation as well as the bug report Without AI
